title: The man who invented twenty-seven spies and fooled Hitler
hook: A Spanish man invented twenty-seven spies, and Germany paid every one.
summary: Juan Pujol García, rejected by Britain, became a German spy, invented a network of fake agents from Lisbon, and helped hide the D-Day landings; he got medals from both sides.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia: Juan Pujol García (Garbo): Spanish, rejected by British, recruited by Abwehr 1941, invented fictitious network, ran in Lisbon then Britain.
Britain's National Archives / MI5: Garbo's false reports about Normandy as a diversion kept German forces at Pas de Calais; he received the Iron Cross and an MBE.

lines.text: A Spanish man invented twenty-seven spies, and Germany paid every one.
lines.caps: A *Spanish man | invented *27 spies, | and Germany *paid | *every one

lines.text: Britain refused him, so Juan Pujol offered to spy for Germany.
lines.caps: Britain *refused him, | so *Pujol offered | to spy for *Germany

lines.text: He stayed in Lisbon, copying from guidebooks.
Then he invented agents, and Berlin sent money for every one.
lines.caps: He invented *agents, | and Berlin sent *money | for *every one

lines.text: Britain finally hired him. On D-Day, his messages said Normandy was a trick.
lines.caps: Britain *hired him. | On *D-Day, | Normandy was a *trick

lines.text: So German tanks waited for a second invasion that never came.
lines.caps: German *tanks waited | for a second *invasion | that never *came

lines.text: Germany gave him the Iron Cross. Britain gave him an MBE.
Two medals, and not one real spy.

post.caption:
He barely left Lisbon, yet two enemy governments trusted him.
Would you have fallen for his lies?
